detail: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

Robinson has missed Boston's previous three games due to an illness, and it appears he's in danger of missing a fourth consecutive outing Friday. Neemias Queta will continue to start in Robinson's place if he remains sidelined, while Luka Garza and Chris Cenac get more minutes off the bench.

Allen will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a concussion. With the veteran swingman sidelined, Sion James (thigh), Grant Williams and Royce O'Neale are candidates for increased playing time. Allen's next chance to play will come Saturday against Brooklyn.

Smith is dealing with a gastrointestinal illness, so he won't suit up Wednesday versus the Hornets. Without him, Nic Claxton will presumably enter the starting lineup. Zach Collins might also be more involved.

The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

Cunningham won't suit up Friday and will miss a second straight game, and the third of his last five, while dealing with right knee tendinopathy. This means Daniss Jenkins should run the point for Detroit on Friday, while Isaiah Joe could be in line for another start at shooting guard. Cunningham's next chance to return will come Sunday against the Magic.

Curry has missed six consecutive games, including Wednesday's tilt versus Sacramento, due to an oblique abdominal tear he sustained against the Rockets on Nov. 11. The Warriors will provide further updates following the holiday. Golden State has gone 1-4 with Curry sidelined, so hopefully Friday will bear some positive news for the 38-year-old.

Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

Oubre has been performing at a high level of late, scoring at least 15 points in six straight contests, but he could be forced to miss time due to a right hand injury. If he is out, Quenton Jackson could see extra minutes.

McConnell has missed the Pacers' last two games due to left hamstring soreness, and the questionable tag suggests the veteran floor general could be an option Friday. He's not expected to have a big role in most fantasy lineups, though, as he's averaging just 7.0 points, 4.3 assists, and 2.3 rebounds per game in his seven outings off the bench this season.

Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

The fact that Antetokounmpo is probable suggests the star forward should have a decent chance to suit up Friday. He's been playing at a high level lately, recording four consecutive double-doubles and averaging 28.6 points, 12.9 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 1.6 blocks per game since the beginning of November.

Ball exited Wednesday's game against the Thunder and finished with 19 points (7-18 FG, 5-9 3Pt), seven rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 29 minutes. If he's unable to suit up Friday, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon would be in line to see more playing time in the backcourt. That would be a huge downgrade for a Minnesota team that's already missing two key backcourt pieces in Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles).

Reese dropped a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double in the Squadron's win over the Mexico City Capitanes on Saturday and will return to the parent club ahead of its game Monday. Through five regular-season appearances at the NBA level this season, the big man is averaging 1.2 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.4 minutes per tilt.

This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

Embiid has missed the team's last two games due to an illness, but it seems the star big man could return as soon as Friday -- or at least it sounds as if he has a chance to do so. Embiid has been turning things around of late, scoring at least 20 points in four games in a row and averaging 27.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and a combined 2.8 steals-plus-blocks per game over that stretch.

Brown is set to undergo imaging of his hamstring, but all signs point to the star forward being on the verge of another spell on the sidelines. Brown has been out for just three games this season, but if he's forced to miss more time, Dean Wade could see an uptick in his playing time.

Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.
